name: Aaplo Kokan | Seafood Restaurant In Borivali West
description:
*"Aaplo Kokan" – A Coastal Culinary Delight! *
"Aaplo Kokan" is a fantastic family restaurant specializing in authentic coastal and seafood cuisine. One of the most popular seafood restaurants in Borivali West is "Aaplo Kokan" managed by Hotel Sai Taj Hospitality since 2007. This establishment specializes in serving a variety of fish thalis and authentic Malvani cuisine, including in house sweet delights. Here, you can relish dishes like **Malvani Chicken Thali, Chicken Tandoori, Kombadi Vade, Crab Lollipop, Fish Thali, Fish Curry**, and other seafood delicacies, all prepared in a traditional **Malvani Style** using homemade spices.
Experience the true flavors of Malvani home-cooked meals at "Aaplo Kokan" – a paradise for food lovers!

featured_reviews.name: THE SIMPLE SOUL
featured_reviews.review_text:
A jewel worth your moolah! Nestled in the by-lanes of Borivali, this little gem is a sparkler, for sure. Your search for authentic Malvani cuisine ends here.
Be it the use of spices, the freshness of the ingredients, the quantity, the quality and the authenticity...all scream 'Fantastic'!
The thalis are delicious and freshly prepared. They do not scrimp on the fried fish or prawns. In fact, on offer, is a free side of freshly fried bombils with the fish thalis and free kothimbir wadi with the Veg thali on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
The fish is fresh. The solkadi is yummy. The JOWARI BHAKRI is super soft..😋
The Kothimbir wadis are delightful too.
The fish gravy is a tad spicy...not for the faint-hearted. But just the way Malvani cuisine should be.
The fresh lime soda is decent.
The absolute highlight: The modaks, though it was a 20 minute wait.  Fresh. Authentic. Mouth-watering, to say the least. And the drizzle of ghee over the modaks...👌😋😋...oohhlaalaa..next level. A++
The juiciest, most scrumptious modaks you could ever have  eaten.
Definitely worth a return...over and over. If consistency prevails.
Thumbs up!! 👍👌

We tried their halwa mini thali which was a perfect lunch/dinner meal to have one.

The place has indoor and outdoor seating with full on konkan vibe in it.

Do visit this place.

Also they are running one offer on every Tuesday Wednesday Thursday on any full thali you will get bombil fry absolutely free!!

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my second visit to Pangat in Nancy Colony, Borivali. I had a good experience earlier, so I came again on a rainy Friday evening with my family. It took us a good 15 minutes to get a table. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating. This time we chose to sit inside. The place looks classy with minimalistic decor, and I liked the overall ambience.

We started with Veg Manchow Soup, Chicken Kalimiri Kebab, and Crab Lollipop. The soup was perfect for the weather and tasted really good. The Chicken Kalimiri Kebab tasted good and was cooked well, but I found a thread in the last piece, which was really disappointing. The staff took it to the kitchen when we showed it, but there was no response after that from their end. The Crab Lollipop tasted like it was frozen and not freshly made in their kitchen. Definitely not something I would order again.

For the main course, we ordered Veg Thali, Chicken Hyderabadi, Jeera Rice, Chapati, and Rice Bhakri. The thali was nice and filling. The Chicken Hyderabadi had good flavours but I personally felt it could have been a bit spicier. It had more of spinach-like aftertaste. The Rice Bhakri was soft and fresh, which I really liked. The Chapati was good and the Jeera Rice was simple and comforting.

The food overall was decent, but the service needs a lot of improvement. We had to call the staff multiple times just to get water or basic things. Many times, they completely ignored us, which was disappointing. When I raised this with the manager, he just listened and didn’t say anything. I honestly feel service matters as much as the food, and that part really fell short during our visit. I have had a better experience here before, so I do hope they take this feedback positively.

Ratings:
Quality - 3/5
Quantity - 4/5
Service - 3/5
Price - ₹2100 for 4 people

For more mouthwatering food content, don’t forget to follow @chefvaidehipathare on Instagram!

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Today I went to this hotel with my family for a dinner.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pangat is one of those places you walk into with high expectations, especially given its reputation for Malvani thalis and coastal favourites. Having been regular patrons for many years, this place has held a certain nostalgic charm for us, which made our recent visits all the more noticeable in contrast.
We sampled a fairly elaborate spread, including their Bombil Thali, Surmai Thali, Prawns Thali, Mandeli fry, along with add ons like the much talked about Crab Lollypop, Bheja Masala, Kalva Sukka, Chicken Potli Kebab, and also revisited dishes we have enjoyed in the past like the keema pattice, bombil fry, and mutton masala.
While the menu continues to promise a seafood lover’s delight, the overall experience, unfortunately, felt average this time around. The Bombil and Surmai fry had the expected crispness, but lacked that depth of flavour and freshness that truly elevates coastal cuisine. The curries across thalis felt somewhat one dimensional, missing the robust, layered Malvani masala profile one associates with Pangat. Even the basics like chapatis and bhakris, which form the backbone of such meals, could be softer, fresher, and more refined.
On a more specific note, the tisrya masala (dry) felt quite chewy, almost rubbery in texture, taking away from what is otherwise a delightful dish when done right. The solkadhi, too, seemed to miss that refreshing kokam forward tang we have experienced here earlier and elsewhere.
That said, what truly stood out and deserves full credit was the service and hospitality. The staff handled everything with genuine warmth, attentiveness, and honesty. From guiding through the menu to ensuring timely service, their effort and intent were clearly heartfelt, and it did make a meaningful difference to the overall dining experience.
Pangat certainly has the foundation of a great dining destination, and perhaps it is just a matter of revisiting the fundamentals. With a bit more attention to core elements like breads, curries, and flavour balance, it has every potential to regain the consistency and charm it was once known for.
For now, a place that still offers variety, but one we hope will soon rediscover the flavours that made it special for us over the years.

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Since we were craving seafood for dinner, I decided to visit Konkan Kinara with my family. The restaurant had a minimalistic setup. When we arrived around 10:45 PM on a Friday night, the place was almost empty, with just one other table occupied. Since this is a Konkani restaurant, going by the name, I assumed they specialized only in Konkani cuisine. But to my surprise, they also served North Indian and Chinese dishes.

To start our meal, we ordered Manchow Soup. Then, we tried Bombil Fry, which was disappointing. Since this is a Konkani restaurant, I expected the fish to be well-marinated, but it tasted bland. So, I had to ask them to take it away. They were kind enough to serve it again, and this time, the flavors were much better.

Next, we tried Veg Seekh Kebab, which had a nice earthy flavor. The Orange Mojito was fresh and had a unique orange flavor. Then, we ordered Masala Papad, Chicken Thali, Mutton Thali, and Veg Thali. The masala papad was crispy and flavorful. The thalis were wholesome, and I feel one thali is more than enough for one person. With every thali, you have the option to choose between Bhakri, Chapati, or Wade, which adds a nice customization to the meal.

I especially liked the Chicken Thali, which came with bhakri. The bhakri was so soft, and I could tell from the taste that it was freshly made. The Veg Thali was also sufficient and included a sweet dish. To end the meal, we ordered Caramel Custard, which was delicious and properly made.

The staff was polite, but at times, they seemed more focused on watching a cricket match rather than attending to guests. We had to call them multiple times for basic service, like refilling water or checking on our order. A little more attentiveness would have made the experience much better.

The restaurant seemed hygienic to me, and overall, it was a decent experience at Konkan Kinara. If you are in the mood for a meat thali or seafood, you may consider visiting this place.

Dishes ordered: Veg Manchow Soup, Chicken Manchow Soup, Chicken Thali, Fry Bombil, Veg Seekh Kebab, Orange Mojito, Masala Papad, Veg Thali, Mutton Thali and, Caramel Custard.

Quantity - 4/5

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
It has been more than twenty years since I first visited Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar with my family, and it continues to remain a special place for us in Borivali. It is one of those restaurants in Borivali that continues to feel like home because of its food and hospitality.

This time, we began our meal with a bowl of Chicken Manchow Soup. It was served hot, and I enjoyed how it had a bold, flavorful taste without being overpowering. For starters, we ordered Veg Seekh Kebab, Mutton Seekh Kebab, and Chicken Pahadi Tikka. The Veg Seekh Kebab was nice, cooked well, and had the perfect earthy flavour. The Mutton Seekh Kebab was outstanding. It had a silky texture, was well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the chutney. It was not chewy at all, and I really liked how smooth it felt with every bite. The Chicken Pahadi Tikka was equally good. The chicken was tender, juicy, and cooked with a light smokiness that made it enjoyable.

For the mains, I ordered Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka. The dal had a nice garlic tempering with the right amount of cumin, and together with the rice it felt wholesome and comforting. The Chicken Tikka Masala came with soft pieces of chicken in a thick gravy that had a good balance of spices. It went really well with the Tandoori Roti, which was crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. The Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was the last dish. It was mildly spiced, had a smoky taste from the wok, and the flavours were balanced in a way that made it enjoyable till the last bite.

As we were about to finish, we couldn’t resist ordering the Chicken Masala Lollipop, which has always been a family favorite. It was crispy, spicy, and coated beautifully with sauce. It was the highlight of the evening. The chicken inside was fresh and well-cooked, and every bite reminded me why I have loved this dish here for years.

The food at Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar is consistently good, and the staff make the experience even better. They are polite, attentive, and always welcoming. This restaurant is more of a family place, and the presence of a bar only adds to the variety without taking away from its warm atmosphere.

Ratings:
Quality - 4/5
Quantity - 4/5
Service - 4.2/5
Price - ₹5000 for 8 people

For more mouthwatering food content, don’t forget to follow @chefvaidehipathare on Instagram!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing to share my deep disappointment regarding the experience my group of 10 had at your restaurant on 08/05/2026.We arrived late in the evening, well before your stated last order time of 11:45 PM, but were met with significant confusion and poor service.Despite the restaurant being busy, the staff seemed completely unorganised regarding table availability for a group of our size. More concerningly, one particular staff member was openly unfriendly and ignored us repeatedly. When we finally spoke to them, we were dismissed with a blunt statement that no space was available, which contradicted the effort of other staff who were trying to assist us.As a customer, I expected a more professional and welcoming attitude, especially in a service industry. This experience was a poor reflection of your establishment and ruined what was meant to be a pleasant family gathering.Despite arriving before your 11:45 PM last order time, we were treated as an inconvenience. Most concerning was the lack of empathy for the elderly members of our group. Even after a large group vacated a table, your staff left it uncleaned for a long period while our elderly family members were forced to wait standing up.Once seated, the service was aggressive and rude. Staff were literally throwing silverware and plates onto the table to set up. We were repeatedly told that the "cooks have to go home," creating an environment where we felt rushed and unwelcome. As customers arriving within operating hours, it is not our "mistake" to expect a professional dining experience.Your kitchen staff clearly takes pride in their work, but the front-of-house team’s behavior ruined our evening. The service staff himself admitted that people love food here and not the service. I Hope the service for the first customer who dines get well treatment then why the last is always bad  because we choose the late time

Sorry not recommending and not coming again

Strawberry delight: A thick shake with strawberry cream.

They place mineral water bottles on the table by default without asking. There is no mention of free RO water or any option given. Most customers will assume it’s complimentary, but later it gets added to the bill.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Hit-and-miss experience; Great Kebabs but lacking variety
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
Su Swagat is a typical Udupi-run establishment located in Borivali East. While there are some highlights, the overall experience was a bit of a mixed bag for me.
The Good:
Tandoori Chicken Tangdi Kebab: This was the star of the meal! Surprisingly great, well-marinated, and cooked to perfection. If you visit, this is definitely a must-try.
Service: Being an Udupi-managed place, the service is generally quick and efficient.
The Not-So-Good:
Ambience: The interiors feel a bit dated and could definitely use an upgrade to make the dining experience more comfortable and inviting.
Dal Khichadi: Quite ordinary. It lacked the soulful, comforting flavor you’d expect from a staple dish.
Menu Options: As a diner in Maharashtra, I was quite let down to find Maharashtrian cuisine completely missing from the menu. Given the location and the competition, adding some local flavors would go a long way.
Final Verdict:
Go here for the Tandoori starters, but don't expect much in terms of local Maharashtrian food or fancy vibes. It's an okay spot for a quick, no-frills meal.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place with my ex-colleagues, and to be honest, The vibe of the place is great for spending time with family.

We ordered quite a few dishes including prawns masala fry, bombil masala, bombil rawa fry, grilled pomfret, crab lollipop, chicken, and finally prawns biryani.

Talking about the food, the crab lollipop was interesting. It obviously felt like frozen food, but the taste was still good. However, most of the seafood dishes were a little disappointing for us. The fish dishes were not spicy enough and lacked that strong flavor we were expecting. The stuffed pomfret was just okay-okay and felt more like boiled fish rather than properly fried.

We also ordered a chicken dish and specifically requested it to be spicy, but unfortunately, it turned out a bit sweet, and none of us really liked it.

But the highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns biryani. It was really, really good and honestly the best dish we had there.

Overall, the ambience and company made the experience enjoyable, but food-wise, only a few dishes really stood out for us.

featured_reviews.name: hemali kantharia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our go-to family dinner spot for any and every occasion. From small celebrations to casual dinners, this place has always been our first choice. Over time we’ve tried almost everything on the menu, and every visit somehow turns into another food memory with family.

If there are two dishes I would recommend to anyone visiting, it has to be the Bombil Fry and Peri Peri Bombil. They are easily my brother’s and my absolute favourites perfectly crispy, full of flavour, and something we end up ordering almost every single time.

And no meal here feels complete without the Kokum Sarbat or Kokum Soda. That refreshing, tangy punch of flavour just balances the seafood so well and makes the whole experience even better.

Good food, great flavours, and the comfort of family dinners this place truly feels special to us. Easily one of the best seafood restaurants and definitely a spot we’ll keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.name: Mitesh Parmar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was the final restaurant I attended on my trip and a great place to end on.

Unfortunately at the time of our attendance the A/C was not in working order which the manager/owner advised on prior to entering, however we still went in as they had fans going on.

Didn't plan to eat a lot but to take in the delights on offer as again this was a place recommended.

We were given good information by the manager on some of the dishes and on ordering the food arrived after a short time. temperatures were on point and flavours were amazing. The prawn starters were so good, especially the Prawns Garlic Butter, so much so we ordered another tray. I also order the Mutton Chops Ghee Roast and as it sat in front of me my mouth was watering. Spice level on this was perfect, had a nice little kick but was really enjoyable and not in a overpowering way. I found that the chop may have been slightly overdone to my liking, however this didn't take the enjoyment away from it.

The meals ordered were enjoyed by everyone in the party which also included children (they really enjoyed the Prawns Garlic Butter). Pricing of the meals and overall was very reasonable and this place is worth a visit if you have never been. I will look to return here again if I visit Mumbai again.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Nav Kayastha Pangat on a Sunday night and had a great experience. We waited around 10 minutes for a table, and the ambience along with the friendly staff made us feel comfortable right away. The warm Kokum drink is a perfect way to welcome guests!

What we ordered:

Mutton Kheema Pattice: A deep-fried snack with mutton kheema stuffed in mashed potato – absolutely delicious!

Bharleli Bombil: Bombil fish stuffed with green chutney and fried. Tasty, but next time I’d prefer plain bombil with chutney on the side.

Tisrya Kalwan: A unique and flavorful clams gravy that paired perfectly with wade.

The total bill for two came to ₹1400. Prices are on the higher side, but the menu is full of interesting and authentic CKP veg/non-veg dishes. Was this the best Mahrashtrian cuisine? No, not really but it's worth trying!

We started with the Bombil Rawa Fry and Kung Pao Paneer, both of which were delicious. For drinks, the Malhaar Bull Power and Spicy Guava Mary mocktails were refreshing and well-balanced. The Prawns Thali was the highlight of the meal, offering fresh seafood and authentic coastal flavours. We also loved the Kori Rotti and Pulimunchi Pomfret, which brought out the true taste of Mangalorean cuisine.

To end on a sweet note, we had the Kesar Pista Kulfi, and were pleasantly surprised with complimentary Gulab Jamuns. A special mention to the staff, who were extremely friendly, attentive, and made us feel welcome throughout our visit.

If you're a seafood lover or looking to explore authentic Mangalorean and Malvani cuisine, this place is definitely worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Kalyan Revankar
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited this place atleast 2-3 times in the last 2-3 months with family and friends. Trust me, it truly made me feel like that I am having homemade sea food. There ambience has been good.I tried relishing their pomfret, king mackerel and bombil thali, it's all amazing. Quantity they serve is really good. Staff is very polite and they helps you with an option about what to choose from their speciality.. though I didn't try their chicken dishes yet, but they serve amazing bombil potli, prawns potli,mandeli potli and mutton potli. Prices wise also it is very friendly. Over all I had a very good experience visiting this place. Going there early in the evening at around 7:30-8pm is preferrable even on the weekends when all the sea food lovers try and cash on too. Because the place is very tiny. featured_reviews.name: Ameya Banavali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst experience on Diwali day!!
Pity the owners because the server threatened customers that they will hit them and the owners would not say anything

Detailed review
I visited today at 1:50 pm. There were people in waiting outside.
After waiting for 6 minutes, a server came out to inform that there was a notebook kept at the side which the customer had to note down their booking by themselves for (no staff to do this)

After waiting for half an hour in the sweltering heat, we (myself, wife and father in law ) got a seat at the further most corner. The one and only AC in the place was running at full throttle but it failed to provide cooling to the crowded room full of customers.

We had already chosen our choice of orders during our wait outside.

Order for :
- Mutton Thali
- Extra Chapati
- Extra Bhakri
- Bombil Fry
- Chicken Poppers
- Alani Bhaat
- Thumbs up half ltr.

After waiting for another 10 mins seated on the table, the server (same guy as earlier) came and took our order very efficiently. 👍

This was at around 2:30 pm. As it was too late for lunch already, we instructed the waiter to get our orders as soon as they were prepared.

The server promptly got the coldrink and plonked the bottle on the table without serving and left. Then we waited and waited and waited.... And waited some more....
In-between we asked the waiter 5 times about when we could see some food on our table his reply everytime was " bas aa rahaa hai"

So after waiting till 3 pm after my senior citizen father in law started getting agitated, (by this time the bombil had been served to us by a lady). At this point I asked the waiter in a loud voice about rest  of my order, The moment I raised my voice, the waiter started shouting back and threatened to hit me.

When the matter escalated, another guy, seemingly the owner came to our table to sort out the matter , he confessed theybwere short on staff  today (not my problem but still)

The lady also intervened and then on she cooled the situation with prompt service and the required attention.

On the food front
Bombil were oily
Mutton was chewy
Poppers were good
Alani Bhaat was excellent

Trigger points-
- This hotel doesnt even have a working washbasin for customers to rinse post meal. Please bear in mind that these people serve fish.
- The AC is pathetic which brings upon a strange discomfort while eating.
- An uncle is a safari suit who was from the restaurant team and claimed be from some food department told that everything is made fresh.  This explains the chewy undercooked mutton as you need to cook mutton for atleast an hour, and simmer before dishing it out.
-Total bill was 1780.

Post meal review-
- At the time of writing this detailed review I am feeling acidic reflux and so is my wife which indicates the quality of ingredients used.

Dear owners
- Your food is pathetic.
- Your ambience is meh.
- Not to be classist but your service is good probably for the slums, not IC Colony.

P.S. I have also messaged my friend who recommended your restaurant to stay away henceforth.

Happy Diwali!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Malvani Pahunchar for dinner recently. Make sure to reach early as they don’t take reservations — it’s strictly first come, first serve, so waiting time can be expected. They have both AC and non-AC seating sections. In ac section they have sitting of 4 tables so I don't think any large group can accommodate in that non ac is horizontal siting so they can club and sit together.

They serve authentic Malvani cuisine, and their variety of thalis are the main attraction — Surmai, Prawns, Chicken, etc.

We tried the Surmai Thali which included fish fry, sukkat, fish gravy, solkadhi, chutney, fish rassa, rice, and an option of bread (bhakri, vade, or chapati). Overall it was good, though the rassa wasn’t very jhanjhanit/spicy.

Chicken lollipop was spicy and tasty, and the Kombdi Wade tasted quite authentic.

We also tried their new ice cream flavours — Puran Poli, Modak, Jackfruit, and Ratnagiri Hapus Mango. We went for the mango ice cream and it was really good.

Overall, a good dining experience for authentic Malvani food lovers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a pleasant experience at this restaurant. Was seated on the first floor which was air conditioned. Service was pretty prompt even though it was for lunch on a Sunday.

Crab lollipop: This appetiser was the star of the show. Fresh crab with a crispy batter and served alongside mint chutney, although I think another dipping sauce like mustard or tartar would pair better.

Kharda mutton: Mutton prepared in a semi dry gravy dominated with green chilly and coconut. This dish is for those who can handle their spice and pairs well with vade or rice bhakari.

featured_reviews.name: Ankit Latam
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently tried a Malvani Pahunchar restaurant and ordered a chicken platter, chicken dish, prawns, and a bombil thali — and it turned out to be a proper coastal feast.
The chicken platter was generous and full of bold Malvani flavors. The spices were rich without overpowering the natural taste, and every bite had that smoky, masala-coated goodness. The chicken dish itself was cooked beautifully — tender, juicy, and soaked in a thick, aromatic gravy that paired perfectly with bhakri.
The prawns were the highlight for seafood lovers. Fresh, succulent, and cooked just right, they carried that authentic coastal spice blend that hits you with warmth rather than heat. And the bombil thali felt like a complete experience — crispy bombil, flavorful curry, and comforting sides that balanced everything out.
Overall, the meal felt homely yet indulgent — exactly what you hope for when craving Malvani cuisine. If you enjoy bold spices, fresh seafood, and hearty portions, this place definitely delivers.

featured_reviews.name: chinu's kitchen
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited The Big Fish & Co. on 4th January while I was shopping around Dadar with my mom and sister. While shopping nearby, we asked a local person for a good restaurant recommendation, and she suggested this place — and honestly, it turned out to be a great choice.
Right from the entrance, the experience was pleasant. The security guard at the door was very polite and kind. He asked if we had a reservation (we didn’t), but luckily a few tables were available. Since we were just three people, we were seated comfortably without any wait.
The ambience is quite good — warm, comfortable, and very suitable for families and friends. There were absolutely no negative points when it came to the atmosphere. What really touched my heart was the attentiveness of the staff. They listened carefully, were patient, and ensured everything was smooth. The service was quick, with no unnecessary delays, which I truly appreciated.
Coming to the food — it felt very local and authentic, something I personally connect with. The dishes were unique and well-prepared. We ordered tandoori prawns, which were medium-sized and nicely cooked. I also ordered a thali and a crab dish, both of which were absolutely delicious and the dessert tooo it’s new for me being a konkani
Overall, it was worth the visit. Great food, warm service, and a lovely atmosphere. I truly loved the experience and would definitely recommend this place.

A Seafood Disaster – Masooli Restaurant

Visited Masooli expecting good seafood. What we got was very disappointing.

We ordered crab garlic, surmai garlic masala, bombil thecha fry, surmai green masala, rice with plain fish curry, solkadi and lime soda. The only real savior in the entire meal was the surmai green masala. The solkadi and lime soda were fine.

Everything else was a letdown. The fish curry had no tanginess, no salt, no flavour. It tasted flat and unfinished. For a seafood restaurant, getting a basic fish curry wrong is shocking. The crab garlic and bombil thecha fry were also disappointing.

I even called the waiter and asked him to taste the fish curry himself. He did not argue or defend it. He was so sure I was right that he did not even attempt to try it.

Service was good and the waiter was polite and attentive. But good service cannot save bad food.

Prices are high, but the taste does not justify it at all. Very disappointing experience. Would not return.

customer_updates.name: Rahul Surve
customer_updates.text:
The restaurant serves authentic Maharashtrian cuisine, and it was an outstanding experience. We started with Agri Matka and Chulivarcha Chicken, both of which were bursting with flavor. The Agri Matka had that traditional rustic touch, slow-cooked to perfection, while the Chulivarcha Chicken, prepared on a traditional clay stove, was smoky, tender, and incredibly delicious.

For starters, we tried the Prawn Sukka, which was a perfect blend of spices, with succulent prawns cooked in a dry, aromatic masala. It was the ideal start to the meal. We also couldn't resist the Prawn Biryani, which was fragrant and loaded with juicy prawns. The balance of spices and flavors in every dish was just spot on.
Overall, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian food. Every dish was prepared with care, and the flavors stayed true to the region's culinary heritage. I can't wait to go back and try more!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in Dadar, on the busy gokhale road, this non veg restaurant is known for sea food.  Restaurant is clean and well maintained.   Service is also clean and neat.  While sea food is good, chicken items are quite ordinary ( tried chicken biryani, butter chicken - nothing great).  On the other hand prawn dishes were good.  Food preparation is Maharashtrian flavor.   Prices are reasonable.
Peak times and peak days would have some wait time to get the table.  Parking is a major problem,  though they have valet service board, I do know where are going to park your vehicle.   Nearest known parking is near Shivaji Park or Kohinoor mall ( BMC  Parking), both about a kilometer away.  I have had food here about five to six times.  Worth a try.
